## Goal

Build the layered framework crate skeletons in `sw-langtools`, build a hybrid
ISA-scaffolding generator in this repo (`sw-vibe-coding/gen-isa`), and validate
the generator by producing the IBM 1130 quintet (`isa`, `target`, `codegen`,
`asm`, `emulator`) in `sw-comp-history` with round-trip tests passing, asm
round-tripping, and a minimal emulator that runs at least one curated program.

A pilot-frontend hello-world is **out of scope** for this saga (separate future
phase-3 saga).

- **sw-langtools** — `sw-isa-core`, `sw-target-core`, `sw-tir`, `sw-tir-opt`,
  `sw-codegen-core`, future `sw-riscv32i-*`.
- **sw-comp-history** — `sw-{ibm1130,cdp1802,s370,s390}-{isa,target,codegen,asm,emulator}`.
- **sw-embed** — existing `sw-cor24-isa` + future `sw-cor24-{target,codegen}` (retrofit, phase 6).
- **sw-vibe-coding/gen-isa** — THIS repo. Generators only. No generated crates live here.

1	# Porting Guide: Bringing Up a New Target ISA
2	
3	> Status: exploratory draft, not git-tracked. Created 2026-05-08.
4	
5	This is a contributor-facing **cookbook** for adding support for a new target ISA. Read `architecture.md` and `design.md` first so the layering is clear; this doc is the step-by-step.
6	
7	The guide assumes the layered scaffolding (`sw-isa-core`, `sw-target-core`, `sw-codegen-core`, `sw-tir`, `sw-tir-opt`) already exists. If you are **building the very first new ISA** (likely IBM 1130), the scaffolding is being designed alongside your work — see §11.
8	
9	## 0. Strategy: greenfield first, retrofit COR24 last
10	
11	It is **easier and lower-risk** to bring up new ISAs against a fresh layered design than to retrofit COR24 first. Reasons:
12	
13	- COR24 is ISA #1; if we use it to validate the abstraction, we'll bake COR24-isms into the trait surface (3-bit register fields, byte-addressed memory, ROM-based encoding, pipelined branch base = PC+4). The abstraction will then strain when ISA #2 doesn't share these properties.
14	- COR24 keeps working **untouched** while the new layering matures. No regressions to manage.
15	- Letting 2–3 new ISAs drive the design produces a trait surface forged against real diversity. By the time we retrofit COR24, the design is stable and the retrofit is mechanical.
16	
17	So the order is:
18	
19	1. Build minimal scaffolding crates (just enough for the first new ISA).
20	2. Bring up the first new ISA (IBM 1130 recommended — it scores highest on the abstraction-disruption axis defined in `architecture.md §6.1`; this is *not* the same as "absolute hardest" — S/390 is harder in absolute terms but is the wrong choice for early validation).
21	3. Bring up additional ISAs (CDP1802, RISC-V I32) — each will push back on the design; iterate.
22	4. Retrofit COR24 once the trait surface has survived 2–3 ISAs.
23	
24	This guide is structured around step 2 (your first new ISA) and 3 (subsequent ISAs). For step 4, see `plan.md §8`.
25	
26	## 1. Prerequisites
27	
28	Before starting, gather:
29	
30	- [ ] **ISA reference manual.** Authoritative source for opcodes, encodings, instruction formats, and machine state. For each planned ISA:
31	  - **IBM 1130:** *IBM 1130 Functional Characteristics* (GA26-5881) and *IBM 1130 Subroutine Library* (manuals are on bitsavers.org).
32	  - **RCA CDP1802:** *RCA Solid State '76 Databook* and *User Manual for the CDP1802 COSMAC Microprocessor* (MPM-201).
33	  - **IBM S/370:** *IBM System/370 Principles of Operation* (GA22-7000).
34	  - **IBM S/390:** *IBM ESA/390 Principles of Operation* (SA22-7201).
35	  - **RISC-V I32:** *RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume I: Unprivileged ISA*.
36	- [ ] **Sample programs in machine code.** A handful of known-good byte sequences and their disassembly, for round-trip validation.
37	- [ ] **An existing emulator** (preferably open-source) for spot-checking your decoder output. SimH covers many historical ISAs; spike covers RISC-V.
38	- [ ] **Reference implementations.** For IBM 1130 specifically, three locally-cloned projects provide cross-check material. **For code reuse, prefer the two MIT-licensed projects (`ibm-1130-rs`, `demo-ibm-1130-system`) -- the user controls those licenses. Treat `S1130` as read-only reference; do NOT port or copy its code.**
39	  - [`sw-comp-history/ibm-1130-rs`](https://github.com/sw-comp-history/ibm-1130-rs) (MIT) -- Rust browser-based educational emulator with interactive assembler. **Primary code-reuse reference** for CPU and assembler. CPU in `src/cpu/{instruction,executor,state,assembler}.rs`; memory and register layout in `docs/architecture.md` (4K words, XR1-3 memory-mapped at addresses 1-3, flags C/V/P/Z).
40	  - [`softwarewrighter/demo-ibm-1130-system`](https://github.com/softwarewrighter/demo-ibm-1130-system) (MIT) -- Rust+WASM **peripheral** simulator (no CPU). **Primary code-reuse reference** for any peripheral support. 153	### 3.3 `decode.rs`
154	
155	Define instruction structs and a `decode` function. Variable-length ISAs return `(Instruction, bytes_consumed)`:
156	
157	```rust
158	pub struct Short { pub op: Opcode, pub tag: u8, pub disp: i8 }
159	pub struct Long  { pub op: Opcode, pub tag: u8, pub indirect: bool, pub address: u16 }
160	pub enum Instruction { Short(Short), Long(Long) }
161	
162	pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(Instruction, usize), DecodeError> {
163	    if bytes.len() < 2 { return Err(DecodeError::Truncated); }
164	    let word = u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1]]); // big-endian for 1130
165	    let f_bit = (word >> 10) & 1;
166	    if f_bit == 0 {
167	        // short form, 1 word
168	        Ok((Instruction::Short(decode_short(word)), 2))
169	    } else {
170	        // long form, 2 words
171	        if bytes.len() < 4 { return Err(DecodeError::Truncated); }
172	        let addr = u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[2], bytes[3]]);
173	        Ok((Instruction::Long(decode_long(word, addr)), 4))
174	    }
175	}
176	```
177	
178	**Pitfalls:**
179	
180	- **Endianness.** Big-endian for IBM, CDP1802, S/370, S/390. Little-endian for RISC-V. COR24 is byte-stream (no endianness applies). Be explicit; don't rely on host byte order.
181	- **Bit-field positions.** Document them in source comments next to the decode logic. Future readers (including you) need them.
182	- **Sign extension.** Displacement fields are usually signed; explicitly cast `i8`, `i16`, `i32` rather than relying on integer-promotion rules.
183	
184	### 3.4 `encode.rs`
185	
186	Inverse of decode. **Round-trip is the test:** `decode(encode(x)) == x`.
187	
188	```rust
189	pub fn encode(insn: &Instruction, out: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, EncodeError> {
190	    match insn {
191	        Instruction::Short(s) => {
192	            if out.len() < 2 { return Err(EncodeError::BufferTooSmall); }
193	            let word = ((s.op as u16) << 11)
194	                     | (0 << 10) // F = 0
195	                     | ((s.tag as u16) << 8)
196	                     | ((s.disp as u8 as u16) & 0xFF);
197	            out[0..2].copy_from_slice(&word.to_be_bytes());
198	            Ok(2)
199	        }
200	        Instruction::Long(l) => { /* … */ }
201	    }
202	}
203	```
204	
205	**Pitfall — don't copy COR24's table-driven encoding.** COR24 encodes via a `(opcode, ra, rb) → byte` perfect-hash because the hardware decoder is itself a ROM (`dis_rom.v`). **No other ISA has this property.** Encode positionally via bit-field assembly. Save the table-driven approach for ISAs whose hardware *actually* uses an external decode ROM.

437	## 9. What to copy from `sw-cor24-isa` and what NOT to copy
438	
439	This is the cherry-pick guide.
440	
441	### COPY
442	
443	- **Module organisation.** Five files: `opcode.rs`, `register.rs`, `branch.rs`, `encode.rs`, `lib.rs` (plus `decode.rs`, `format.rs` as needed). Same names, same responsibilities.
444	- **Public API style.** Small free functions, fieldless enums with `From<u8>`, `Display`, `mnemonic()`, `format()`. Idiomatic and predictable.
445	- **`Cargo.toml` shape.** Same package metadata layout, same optional `serde` feature gate.
446	- **Documentation tone.** Short doc comments, no marketing prose, code-comment-style explanations of bit fields.
447	- **`branch.rs` structure.** Constants + `can_short_branch` helper. Adjust the constants; keep the shape.
448	- **Test patterns.** `#[test] fn test_encode_X` per opcode; round-trip helper.
449	- **License + COPYRIGHT files.**
450	
451	### DO NOT COPY
452	
453	- **The encoding table mechanism.** `sw-cor24-isa::encode::encode_instruction` is a 300-line `match (opcode, ra, rb)` table because COR24's hardware decoder is a ROM (`dis_rom.v`). For every other planned ISA, instructions encode positionally via bit-field assembly. Use `(value << shift) | mask` arithmetic, not exhaustive tables.
454	- **The 5-bit-opcode-via-decoded-rom convention.** COR24's `Opcode::from_decoded` reads bits 10..6 of a 12-bit ROM output. This is COR24-specific. Other ISAs read opcode bits directly from the instruction word.
455	- **The `(ra=7, rb=7) = no-op-operands` convention.** COR24 uses unused register fields to fill encoding slots. Other ISAs encode these positions semantically.
456	- **The 3-bit register field assumption.** COR24 has 8 registers. Don't generalise the bit width — declare the register type per ISA.
457	- **The `BRANCH_PIPELINE_DELAY = 4` and `branch_base = PC + 4` semantics.** This reflects COR24's 3-prefetch + 1-execute pipeline. Most ISAs use PC-relative-to-next-instruction or PC-relative-to-current-instruction. Match your ISA's actual behaviour.
458	- **Byte-addressed memory assumptions in any helper that touches addresses.** IBM 1130 is word-addressed; functions like "advance address by 1 instruction" must respect `AddressUnit`.
459	- **The `MAX_INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 4` constant value.** S/370 has 6-byte instructions; CDP1802 has 1–3 byte instructions. Set per ISA.
460	
461	### LOOK AT BUT REIMPLEMENT
462	
463	- **`opcode::Opcode::format()`** — the *idea* of mapping opcodes to a format enum is universal; the contents are per-ISA.
464	- **Test fixture style** — `tests/encode_decode.rs` patterns transfer; the actual vectors don't.
465	- **`reg_name` and `parse_register`** — same concept, different table.

467	## 10. Common pitfalls per ISA family
468	
469	| ISA family | Pitfall | Mitigation |
470	| ---------- | ------- | ---------- |
471	| Word-addressed (IBM 1130) | Forgetting that `address + 1` advances by 2 bytes | Use the `AddressType::step` API; never hand-arithmetic byte counts |
472	| Accumulator-only (1130, CDP1802) | Naive register allocator runs out of registers immediately | Set `RegisterClasses::gpr()` correctly; expect heavy spilling; consider custom allocator |
473	| Indirect-via-register-pair (1130 Long form, S/370 RX) | Forgetting that the register operand is a *pointer*, not a value | Decode and encode operand semantics carefully; document indirect bits |
474	| Multi-format (S/370) | Conflating format with opcode | Keep `Format` orthogonal to `Opcode`; format determines size and operand layout |
475	| Variable-length (most non-RISC-V) | Off-by-one on bytes consumed | Always return bytes consumed from `decode`; assert in tests |
476	| Fixed-length 32-bit (RISC-V I32) | Confusion between u32 instruction word and the 4 bytes | Pick one (we use bytes throughout) and stick with it |
477	| Big-endian (IBM, CDP1802, S/370) | Host byte order leakage | Use `u16::from_be_bytes` / `to_be_bytes`; never transmute |
478	| Pipelined branch base (COR24-style) | Off-by-N on branch offset semantics | Document the branch base in `branch.rs`; cite the manual |

# IBM 1130 ABI

Status: invented for this toolchain. The IBM 1130 manuals do not specify
a calling convention -- routine entry/exit was per-program in the era's
assembly idiom, and the FORTRAN/CALL subroutine library used its own
conventions tied to IBM's runtime. This document defines the ABI that
`sw-ibm1130-target`, `sw-ibm1130-codegen`, and downstream code agree
on.

References:

- `gen-isa/docs/decisions.md` Sec 1 (XR3 reserved as frame pointer).
- `gen-isa/docs/porting-guide.md` Sec 5 (ABI invention guidance).
- IBM 1130 Functional Characteristics (GA26-5881) for hardware register
  state and instruction semantics.

ASCII-only by convention.

## 1. Machine state recap

The 1130 has six addressable registers from the toolchain's point of
view (see `sw-ibm1130-isa::register::Reg`):

| Reg  | Width | Hardware role                                  |
| ---- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------- |
